subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: For provider-minted signed-thinking fields, should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid opaque replay tokens even when their bytes contain credential-shaped substrings, and pair that with Bedrock/Anthropic poisoned-block cleanup?
rationale: The current tests deliberately redact credential-shaped provider signature fields, but the report shows that policy can corrupt real opaque replay tokens; changing it adjusts the transcript secret-redaction boundary.

options.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
options.body: Preserve only validated opaque signatures in known provider signed-thinking fields while keeping arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

options.title: Pattern-Only Hardening
options.body: Tighten fixed-case vendor prefixes and boundaries but keep the current redaction-idempotency requirement for provider signatures.

options.title: Send-Side Recovery Only
options.body: Drop visibly corrupted Bedrock/Anthropic thinking blocks before replay without changing transcript-redaction preservation.

recommendation.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve only validated opaque signatures in known provider signed-thinking fields while keeping arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and release history point to this person across the active redaction and Bedrock replay surfaces.
